requirements.text: The coach's exit safety signs shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 6.5 of ISO 3864-1:2011.
Each safety sign on the coach shall communicate only one safety message.
Each required safety sign shall be located and orientated so as to be easily understood.
Where supplementary words, single letters or numbers appear on a safety sign, their lower case characters shall have a minimum height of 8 mm.
All safety signs visible from inside the passenger compartment shall be made of photo-luminescent material.
The photo-luminescent safety signs shall have luminance decay characteristics conforming at least to sub-classification C in Table 2 of ISO 17398:2004.
The safety signs shall not be located where they may be obscured during operation of the vehicle.
Each emergency exit of the coach shall be marked by one of the relevant pictograms of Table 3 of ISO 7010:2011.
The exit pictograms shall be legible from both the inside and the outside of the vehicle.
Safety signs shall be positioned adjacent to, surrounding, or on every internal and external emergency control and on every emergency-window breaking device.
No part of a safety sign shall obscure any misuse protection such as a protective cover.
Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall illuminate a flat horizontal ground portion 2 m wide measured from a plane parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal vertical plane.
Service-door lighting, if fitted, shall have limited dazzle outside a ground zone of maximum width 5 m measured from the side of the vehicle.
Where a service-door lighting device has its lower edge less than 2 m from the ground, it shall not project more than 50 mm beyond the overall vehicle width.
Service-door lighting shall be installed so that it can only be switched on when a service door is operated and the vehicle speed does not exceed 5 km/h.
Service-door lighting shall switch off automatically before the vehicle reaches a speed exceeding 5 km/h.
The free space extending inwards from the side wall in which a service door is mounted shall permit the free passage of test gauge 1 or test gauge 2 as specified in Annex 4, Figure 1.
The maximum slope of the floor in each access passage shall not exceed 5 per cent.
The surface of the access passages shall be slip-resistant.
The free space between the gangway and each emergency door aperture shall permit the free passage of the specified vertical dual-cylinder assembly 1,400 mm high.
The base of the lower cylinder used for emergency door access shall lie within the projection of the upper cylinder.
It shall be possible to move a test gauge from the gangway to the exterior of the vehicle through every emergency window.
The emergency-window access test gauge shall be a thin plate 600 mm x 400 mm with corners radiused by 200 mm.
At least one roof escape hatch shall be located so that the specified four-sided truncated pyramid 1,600 mm high touches part of a seat or equivalent support.
The coach gangway shall be designed and constructed to permit the free passage of the two-coaxial-cylinder gauging device of Annex 4, Figure 6.
Where monitor or display devices are mounted from the ceiling above the gangway of a Class III coach, the maximum force to move them out of the way shall not exceed 35 N.
A gangway-mounted monitor or display device, once moved out of the way, shall maintain its position and shall not automatically redeploy.
Where laterally movable seats are fitted in the Class III coach, the gangway width may be reduced to correspond to a lower cylinder diameter of 220 mm.
Folding seats allowing passengers to sit in the gangway shall not be fitted in the coach.
The surface of the coach gangways shall be slip-resistant.
The longitudinal slope of the gangway of the Class III coach shall not exceed 12.5 per cent.
The transversal slope of the coach gangway shall not exceed 5 per cent.
Where the coach has a transition from a sunken gangway to a seating area, the vertical distance between the gangway surface and the seating-area floor shall not exceed 350 mm.
Where more than one step is provided, each step may extend into the vertical projection of the next step by up to 100 mm while leaving a free tread surface of at least 200 mm.
All step nosings of the coach shall be designed to minimise the risk of tripping.
For the coach carrying more than 22 passengers, a rectangle of 400 mm x 300 mm shall be placeable on the first step with not more than 5 per cent overhang.
For the coach carrying more than 22 passengers, a rectangle of 400 mm x 200 mm shall be placeable on each other step with not more than 5 per cent overhang.
All passenger steps of the coach shall have a slip-resistant surface.
The maximum slope of each step in any direction shall not exceed 5 per cent.
All step nosings shall have a band of contrasting colour on the front edge of the tread.
The contrasting colour band on each step nosing shall be 20 to 50 mm wide and provide a visual contrast C ≥ 0.7 and diffuse reflectance ρd of at least 0.5.
The minimum seat cushion width F of each passenger seat in the Class III coach shall be 225 mm measured from the centre plane of the seating position.
The minimum available space width G for each individual passenger seat shall be 250 mm at heights between 270 mm and 650 mm above the uncompressed cushion.
The minimum available space width G for each position in continuous rows of seats shall be 225 mm at heights between 270 mm and 650 mm above the uncompressed cushion.
The minimum depth K of each passenger seat cushion in the Class III coach shall be 400 mm.
The height of each uncompressed passenger seat cushion relative to the floor shall be between 400 mm and 500 mm.
Where a passenger seat is over a wheel arch or the engine/transmission compartment, the cushion height may be reduced to not less than 350 mm.
For same-direction seats, the horizontal distance H between the front of a seat squab and the back of the squab of the preceding seat shall not be less than 680 mm.
Seat spacing shall be measured with the cushion and squab uncompressed using the test gauge of Annex 4, Figure 12B.
Where transverse seats face one another, the minimum distance between the front faces of the squabs shall be not less than 1,300 mm.
Seat dimension measurements shall be taken with reclining and adjustable seats in the normal position of use specified by the manufacturer.
For each seat behind a seat or facing the gangway, a minimum clear foot space of at least 300 mm depth shall be provided.
Where the Class III coach is subject to the requirements of Annex 8, at least two priority seats complying with Annex 8 paragraph 3.2 shall be provided.
Over each seating position and its foot space, the free height shall be at least 900 mm above the uncompressed cushion and at least 1,350 mm above the floor.
The free space over each seating position shall extend between longitudinal vertical planes 200 mm either side of the seat's median vertical plane.
For upper outboard seats adjacent to the inner wall, a rectangular zone 150 mm high and 100 mm wide may be excluded from the free space.
A wheel arch intrusion into the free space of an outboard seat is permitted where it does not extend beyond the median vertical plane of the seating position.
Every door to a toilet or other interior compartment in the coach shall be self-closing and shall not be fitted with a device to hold it open where it could obstruct passengers in an emergency.
Every interior-compartment door, when open, shall not conceal any handle, opening control or obligatory marking of a service door, emergency door or other emergency exit.
Every door to a toilet or other interior compartment shall be provided with a means to open it from outside the compartment in an emergency.
Where a guard is fitted behind the driver's compartment, its minimum height measured from the passenger's floor shall be 800 mm.
The coach shall be designed so that a 50 mm diameter ball cannot roll into the driver's compartment from the passenger area immediately behind it.
The minimum width F of the driver's seat cushion in the Class III coach shall be 225 mm.
The minimum depth K of the driver's seat cushion shall be 400 mm.
The minimum overall width of the driver's seat back up to 250 mm above the uncompressed cushion shall be 450 mm.
The driver's seat shall be adjustable longitudinally, vertically and in backrest inclination and shall lock automatically in the selected position.
Internal electrical lighting shall illuminate the access to every exit and the area immediately around each service door.
Internal electrical lighting shall illuminate the internal markings and internal controls of all exits.
The coach shall have at least two internal lighting circuits such that failure of one does not affect the other.
The Class III coach shall allow the driver to activate the emergency lighting system from the driver's seating position.
Operating the emergency control of any service or emergency door shall activate the emergency lighting system.
The emergency lighting system, once activated, shall remain active for at least 30 minutes unless de-activated by the driver.
All units providing the emergency lighting shall produce white light.
The emergency lighting system shall provide at least 10 lux directly under each light unit at 750 mm above the gangway centreline.
The emergency lighting uniformity over the passenger compartment at 750 mm above access passages and gangways shall be between 0.15 and 2.
The emergency lighting system shall provide at least 1 lux at floor level on the centreline of all access passages and gangways.
The interior handrails and handholds of the coach shall be of adequate strength.
The handrails and handholds shall be designed and installed so as to present no risk of injury to passengers.
Every interior handrail shall provide a grasping length of at least 100 mm to accommodate a hand.
No cross-section dimension of a handrail or handhold shall be smaller than 20 mm or greater than 45 mm, except for handrails on doors and seats and in access passages.
The interior handrails shall not have sharp bends.
The clearance between a handrail or handhold and the adjacent vehicle body or wall shall be at least 40 mm along the majority of its length.
The surface of every handrail, handhold and stanchion shall contrast visually with its surroundings and have a diffuse reflectance ρd of at least 0.5.
Alternatively, the surface of every handrail, handhold and stanchion shall be yellow or white.
The surface of every handrail, handhold and stanchion shall be slip-resistant.
Each service door aperture shall be fitted with handrails and/or handholds on both sides.
The service-door grasping points shall be situated vertically between 800 mm and 1,100 mm above the ground or above the surface of each step.
The coach manufacturer shall specify means to transmit safety information to passengers, adapted to the vehicle design and intelligible from any passenger seat.
Where a fire suppression system is fitted, it shall be automatically activated through a fire detection system.
All cables of the heating and emergency-lighting harness shall be well insulated and shall withstand the temperature and humidity conditions to which they are exposed.
Every electrical circuit feeding the heating blower, controls or emergency lighting shall include a fuse or a circuit breaker.
All cables shall be well protected and held securely in position so that they cannot be damaged by cutting, abrasion or chafing.
All electrical cables shall be located so that no part contacts a fuel line or any part of the exhaust system or is subjected to excessive heat.
No flammable material shall be located within 100 mm of the heating system components, exhaust system, high-voltage equipment or any other significant heat source unless effectively shielded.
A partition of heat-resisting material shall be fitted between the heating system or any other heat source other than a warm-water device and the rest of the vehicle.
Where a passenger-compartment heating device operates other than by hot water, it shall be encased in material that resists the temperatures it generates.
A non-hot-water passenger-compartment heating device shall emit no toxic fumes and shall be positioned so that no passenger is likely to contact a hot surface.
Space shall be provided for fitting one or more fire extinguishers, one being near the driver's seat.
Space of not less than 7 dm3 shall be provided for fitting one or more first-aid kits, with a minimum dimension of not less than 80 mm.
The coach occupants shall be protected from objects liable to fall from the luggage racks under braking or cornering forces.
Where luggage compartments are fitted, they shall be designed so that baggage is prevented from falling in the event of sudden braking.
Any floor trap door that is not an escape hatch shall have no lifting or securing device projecting more than 8 mm above floor level, and the edges of such projections shall be rounded.
Any visual entertainment monitors for passengers shall be located out of the driver's view when the driver is seated in the normal driving position.
Where the coach is delivered with a driver's compartment without a roof, the driver shall be provided with special protection against strong wind, dust and heavy rain.
When the service-door access test gauge has traversed 300 mm from its starting position and touches the step or floor, it shall be retained in that position for verification.
A service-door handhold grasping point for a person on the ground shall be not more than 400 mm inwards from the outer edge of the first step.
For seats adjacent to the coach wall, the available space at shoulder height may exclude a triangular area 20 mm wide by 100 mm high.
Upon detection of excess temperature or smoke in a separate compartment, the alarm system shall give the driver an acoustic and a visual signal and activate the hazard warning signal.
